Years ago, hackers broke into @AutoDsTools and changed every customer's username overnight.

I went live on Facebook the same day. 
Walked everyone through what happened.

Zero customers left.

Real brands aren't built when everything works. 
They're built on what breaks.

Was it the team's fault? Absolutely.

Most founders would have hidden in their Slack DMs and quietly rebuilt.

Crane did the opposite. He posted a long, public breakdown on X. It went viral.

His authority only grew from there.

3 things to learn from this:

→ Minimum permissions only. Separate tokens for staging and production.

→ Backups off-service. If your AI can delete the data, it shouldn't be able to delete the backup.

→ Post your failures. Take ownership.

3 things I learned after 2 weeks using Paperclip:

1. The dashboard is legit.
If you're juggling 5 Claude Code terminals, Paperclip solves a real problem.

2. The org chart kills the output.
CEO tells CTO, CTO tells engineer.
By the time the work comes back, it's a blurry copy of a blurry copy of what you asked for.

3. AI can do everything except know your values.
You still have to encode the taste and the judgment yourself.

Real people push back.
Agents don't. They just execute the drift.

Paperclip is great software.
But zero human company? Not yet.
